hypothesis: Caching the Neo4j SessionConfig as a private val (built once at init) and using explicit READ/WRITE AccessMode should reduce avg_latency_us by 10-20% by eliminating per-call SessionConfig builder allocation and enabling Bolt routing optimization for read ops.

steps.change: Import org.neo4j.driver.AccessMode. Replace the per-call session() helper with two cached SessionConfig fields built once at class init: `private val readSessionConfig = SessionConfig.builder().withDatabase(database).withDefaultAccessMode(AccessMode.READ).build()` and `private val writeSessionConfig = SessionConfig.builder().withDatabase(database).withDefaultAccessMode(AccessMode.WRITE).build()`. Add two helpers: `private fun readSession(): Session = driver.session(readSessionConfig)` and `private fun writeSession(): Session = driver.session(writeSessionConfig)`.

Split `runQuery` into `runReadQuery` (uses readSession()) and `runWriteQuery` (uses writeSession()). Route read-only methods (findVertexById, findVerticesByLabel, findEdgesByLabel, countVertices, graphExists, neighbors, shortestPath, traversal BFS/DFS, pageRank, components, cycles, degrees) through readSession/runReadQuery. Route mutating methods (createVertex, updateVertex, deleteVertex, createEdge, deleteEdge, dropGraph) through writeSession/runWriteQuery. Keep the public API unchanged.

Apply the same refactor to the Suspend variant. Cache `readSessionConfig` and `writeSessionConfig` as private vals with `AccessMode.READ` and `AccessMode.WRITE` respectively. Provide `readSession()` and `writeSession()` factory helpers returning ReactiveSession. Split runQuery/flowQuery into read/write variants and route each override accordingly. Preserve the existing NonCancellable close semantics.

Run the existing Neo4j sync and suspend test suites (and LinkedIn/code-graph example tests that target Neo4j) to confirm the read/write session routing does not alter observable behavior. No test changes are expected; this step only verifies correctness of the refactor via `./gradlew :graph-neo4j:test` and `./gradlew :code-graph-examples:test --tests '*Neo4j*'`.

Run the existing Neo4j JMH benchmarks (Sync + VirtualThread + Suspend) before and after the change with the same dataset size to capture avg_latency_us. Record baseline vs optimized numbers in the round_2 results artifact. No code changes to the benchmark class unless a new benchmark method is needed to isolate read-heavy workloads.

expected_outcome.rationale: Every session() call currently allocates a fresh SessionConfig via the builder (object allocation + immutable copy). Moving to two cached SessionConfig instances removes this per-operation allocation. More importantly, setting AccessMode.READ on read sessions allows the Bolt driver to skip leader routing and use a reader server directly (in clustered deployments) and also enables Neo4j server-side to route queries to read replicas, lowering latency. On a single-instance test container the gain comes primarily from builder allocation removal and reduced GC pressure during benchmark hot loops; the routing benefit is latent but becomes significant in production topologies.

sub_score_expectations.avg_latency_us: reduce by 10-20% across findVertexById / findVerticesByLabel / neighbors
sub_score_expectations.allocation_rate: reduced due to elimination of per-call SessionConfig builder + immutable config object
sub_score_expectations.throughput_ops_per_sec: small increase (3-8%) proportional to latency reduction
sub_score_expectations.correctness: unchanged — all existing tests must pass

history_reference.builds_on: Round 1 planner_c (Neo4j ReactiveSession refactor) passed all tests — this is a complementary optimization that reuses the session-lifecycle pattern already validated and layers SessionConfig caching + AccessMode routing on top of it.

architect_review.feedback: Cached SessionConfig + explicit AccessMode is a well-known Neo4j driver optimization. Refactor is local to two files, preserves the public GraphOperations/GraphSuspendOperations contract, and keeps session lifecycle semantics intact. Low structural risk.
